topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Genetic, Endogenous, and Inherited Origins of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by intrinsic cellular processes, replication errors, and inherited genetic susceptibilities.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Epidemiological Patterns, and the Cancer Risk Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine external environmental exposures, global epidemiological variations, and the ongoing debate surrounding environmental causes versus chance mutations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how infectious agents promote malignant transformation, detailing the viral and environmental mechanisms underlying Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and dietary or environmental chemicals induce DNA damage directly or following host metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Developmental Susceptibility, and Carcinogenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental timing collaborate with initiators to facilitate cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to establish whether agents are mutagenic and carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks on balancing exposure risks against everyday practical benefits.
